files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
Notes become a design review: resolve a note when it is dealt with, answer it in a thread, and @mention a colleague, who is notified and taken straight to it. Print check now says what is wrong with a mesh (holes, faces the wrong way, inside-out parts) and repairs it, saving the mended STL or 3MF next to the model. And a model's size, triangle count, parts and notes show in a 3D tab in the Files sidebar, without opening it.

### Added
- Repair a model for printing: Print check now lists what is wrong with the mesh, in plain words (holes and their open edges, faces that point the wrong way, a part that is inside out, vertices that almost meet but do not, faces with no area, repeated faces, and edges shared by more than two faces), and when something can be mended, offers Repair. Repair joins the vertices, drops faces with no area and repeated faces, turns faces and whole parts the right way out, and fills the holes whose edge is a simple loop, then says what it did ("Joined 1,204 vertices", "Turned 36 faces the right way", "Filled 3 holes") and what it left and why ("1 hole is too large to fill", "4 edges are shared by more than two faces"). On a model of more than 100,000 triangles this is checked when you press "Check the mesh for problems", so Print check opens as lightly as before. The closed-model check runs again on the result, so the card shows the new state and a model that was open now gets its filament estimate. Vertices are joined only when they are closer than a tolerance worked out from the model's size and its unit, never more than a micron, so the fine detail of a small millimetre part is kept. It does not remove self-intersections or remesh. The repaired model never replaces the one on screen or the file: what the repair filled is drawn over the model in green, and "Undo repair" puts the card back as it was.
- Get the repaired file: "Save repaired STL next to the model" (or 3MF, as chosen) writes it into the model's own folder as "bracket (repaired).stl", numbered if that name is taken and never replacing a file, for someone logged in who may add files to the folder; otherwise, and always, "Download repaired STL" gives it as a download, wherever Export does. It is written the way Export writes the model, at the model's real size and unit. Not offered for point clouds, Gaussian splats or G-code.
- Notes can be resolved and answered, so they work as a design review. Anyone who may add notes to a model can mark a note resolved, with a note that says who resolved it and when, and open it again. A resolved note stays in the list, marked as resolved, and its marker in the scene is hidden until "Show resolved notes in the scene" is ticked, which draws it dimmed. Above the list, All, Open and Resolved show how many notes each holds. Every note on a model before this update is open. Measurements and angles can be resolved too.
- A note has a thread of replies, shown under it in the order they were written, each with who wrote it and when. Anyone who may add notes to the model can reply, and, as with the notes themselves, edit or delete any reply under it. A reply to a resolved note leaves it resolved: answering "done, thanks" is not a reason to put the note back on someone's list, and Reopen is its own button. Deleting a note deletes its replies. People who can only view the model, and visitors on a public link, read the thread but cannot change it.
- Typing @ in a note's text or in a reply offers the people who can open the model, from Nextcloud's own people search, so it follows the same rules about who may be listed to whom as the share dialog. The person you pick is shown by name, in the field, in the thread and in the label in the scene, while the note keeps their account id, so the mention still means the same person after a rename. A person who is mentioned, and can open the model, gets a notification "Someone mentioned you in a note on bracket.step" that opens the model at that note, with its thread. A name is only ever turned into a person who can open the model and whom Nextcloud's people search lets you find, so a mention cannot be used to find out who has an account or what they are called: anyone else stays plain text, the same for an account that does not exist as for one you may not see, and the administrator's sharing and user-enumeration settings (including "only share with group members") apply. Nobody who cannot open the model is told, you are never told about your own mentions, and someone who would also have been told a note was added is told of the mention only. A note's text is saved as it is typed, so a name at the very end of it counts as a mention once something follows it.
- Resolving, reopening and replying show in the Activity stream of everyone who can open the model, under the 3D Viewer filter, as adding a note does ("Omar resolved a note on bracket.step", "You replied to a note on bracket.step"). Neither the stream nor a notification says what a note or a reply says. The setting under Settings › Notifications now reads "Notes on a 3D model were added, changed, resolved, replied to or deleted".
- On a public link, notes show whether they are resolved and the replies under them, read-only. No name appears: not who wrote a reply, not who resolved the note, and every @word that reads as a mention is shown as "@someone", whether or not it names anyone, and nothing is looked up for it.
- A note's link ("Copy link to this note", and the one in a notification) opens the note with its thread, even if the list is filtered to hide it.
- A "3D" tab in the Files app's sidebar: open the details of a model (the right-hand panel) and the tab shows its format, its size as width × depth × height in the file's own unit, its triangles and vertices (a scan's points, a splat's splats, a G-code file's layers and print time), its parts, materials and textures, and how many notes it has, with a link that opens the model at the first one and an "Open in 3D Viewer" button. When the format records no unit (an STL, say) the tab says the unit is a guess, and says so no longer once someone has set it on the file; a unit chosen later is followed without measuring again. The numbers come from your browser: they are measured while a thumbnail is made, and when a model has none yet the tab measures it itself, within the size and time limits in Personal Settings (a model over them is called too large to measure here, with the button to open it), then keeps the result for everyone who can open the file, so the tab is instant the next time (the result is stored by someone who can edit the file, like a thumbnail; someone who can only read it sees the same numbers, measured in their own browser). They are kept per file version, so an edited model is never shown its older numbers, and they go with the file. It works from the keyboard, follows the theme and the right-to-left layout, and has its own small script, so the Files page loads next to nothing for it until the sidebar is opened. It shows for signed-in users on Nextcloud 31 to 35 (Nextcloud 31 and 32 take a tab one way, 33 and later another, and the app registers with whichever the server has); a public link has no sidebar tab. A `.nc` or `.g` file, which other programs use too, is measured only when you press "Measure this file".

### Fixed
- Retry on a note or measurement that failed to save sent it again but left it marked as not saved, so pressing Retry once more saved a second copy for everyone. A retried note is now marked saved, and saved once.
